'''Weazel''' was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] [[thief]] turned freedom fighter from the [[planet]] [[Tatooine]] who lived in the last days of the [[Galactic Republic]] and during the [[Imperial Era|reign]] of the [[Galactic Empire]]. As a thief, he worked for the [[Hutt Clan]] out of [[Mos Espa]] on [[Tatooine]], where he was present for the [[Boonta Eve Classic]] [[Podracing|podrace]] in [[32 BBY]] that was won by [[Anakin Skywalker]]. During the age of the Empire, Weazel worked with [[Enfys Nest]] and her [[Cloud-Riders]], who sought to fight back against the [[crime lord]]s who had wronged them as well as the Empire. He was Nest's best [[Lieutenant (criminal)|lieutenant]] and most vigilant [[spy]].

==Biography==
===Life as a thief===
[[File:Wattomocks.png|thumb|left|250px|Weazel sat and cheered alongside Watto during the Boonta Eve Classic in 32 BBY.]]
Weazel was [[Homeworld|from]] the [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]] [[Planet|world]] of [[Tatooine]],<ref name="Ultimate Star Wars NE" /> where he worked as a [[thief]] for the ruling [[Hutt Clan]] in the [[spaceport]] settlement of [[Mos Espa]]<ref name="Episode I" /> in [[32 BBY]].<ref name="Episode I date">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' dates the events of [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], which includes the [[Boonta Eve Classic]], to [[32 BBY]].</ref> During the time of the [[Trade Federation]]{{'s}} [[Invasion of Naboo]], Weazel attended the [[Boonta Eve Classic]] [[Podracing|podrace]] in Mos Espa, where he sat with [[Watto]], a [[Toydarian]] junk dealer who placed a large sum of money on the reigning champion [[Sebulba]] to win. Weazel cheered Sebulba on throughout the race, but the [[Dug]] racer was ultimately beaten by the young [[Anakin Skywalker]]<ref name="Episode I" />—the boy who would grow up to become Darth Vader,<ref name="Episode III">{{Film|III}}</ref> the enforcer of the [[Galactic Empire]]<ref name="Episode IV">{{Film|IV}}</ref> that Weazel came to fight against during the [[Imperial Era]].<ref name="Solo">''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story]]''</ref>

===Fighting with the Cloud-Riders===
{{Quote|We're not marauders. We're allies. And the war has just begun.|Enfys Nest|audio=Enfys-Allies.flac|<ref name="Solo" />}}
[[File:Weazel-SoloOMG.png|thumb|right|200px|Weazel, with his K21c portable ordnance launcher]]
By the time the Empire was in power, Weazel had left behind his life as a thief and joined the [[Cloud-Riders]], a group of vigilante marauders led by [[Enfys Nest]].<ref name="Solo Official Guide" /> While rivals such as [[Tobias Beckett]] believed them to be pirate thieves, they were actually aspiring rebels who wanted to fight for and bring justice to those who had been victimized by the Empire and the criminal syndicates that ran rampant in [[the galaxy]], such as [[Crimson Dawn]].<ref name="Solo" /> Weazel became Nest's most trusted [[Lieutenant (criminal)|lieutenant]] and vigilant [[spy]],<ref name="Solo Official Guide" /> and together they and the Cloud-Riders had numerous run-ins with Beckett and [[Beckett's gang|his crew]], who often worked for Crimson Dawn.<ref name="Solo" />

In [[11 BBY]], Weazel accompanied Nest, [[Callixido Ryss]] and [[Moda Maxa]] to [[Gargon]] to [[Raid on Gargon|raid]] an Imperial [[spice]] [[Imperial medical spice cache|cache]] in order to retrieve medicinally processed [[spice]]. The raid succeeded, and the obtained spice was segmented into ready-to-implement triage kits and emergency packs, but they left the raw spice behind even though they could have stolen it to refine it for narcotic usage and make a fortune by selling it. This action surprised [[Agent]] [[Andressa Divo]] of the [[Imperial Security Bureau]], who noted that the Cloud-Riders were likely building an [[army]] and readying to go to war.<ref name="Scum and Villainy">''[[Star Wars: Scum and Villainy: Case Files on the Galaxy's Most Notorious]]''</ref>

The Cloud-Riders had their last run-in with Beckett's gang in [[10 BBY]],<ref name="Solo Official Guide" /> when the Cloud-Riders caught wind of a [[Heist on Vandor|heist]] Beckett and his team were pulling on [[Vandor]] for Crimson Dawn. While Beckett, his partner [[Val]], [[pilot]] [[Rio Durant]], and newcomers [[Han Solo]] and [[Chewbacca]] attempted to steal the hyperfuel known as [[coaxium]] from an Imperial [[20-T Railcrawler conveyex transport|conveyex train]], the Cloud-Riders attacked on [[swoop]] bikes and attempted to steal the loot for themselves. The encounter led to some Cloud-Rider casualties as well as the deaths of Val and Durant. Neither team was able to steal the loot; as each attempted to take the train car carrying the coaxium for themselves, the pilot Solo detached the car from the [[Y-45 armored transport hauler|AT-hauler]] he was flying, and it crashed into a mountain. Weazel and the others survived the resulting massive explosion of hyperfuel, and each went their separate ways.<ref name="Solo" />

[[File:Enfys_Nest_and_company.png|thumb|left|250px|Weazel and the Cloud-Riders, on Savareen]]
Beckett arranged a new operation with Crimson Dawn to steal coaxium from the [[Spice mines of Kessel|spice mines]] of [[Kessel]], an operation the Cloud-Riders also caught wind of. Weazel followed Beckett's team as they met with [[Landonis Balthazar Calrissian|Lando Calrissian]] and arranged for him and his [[YT-1300 light freighter|ship]], the ''[[Millennium Falcon]]'', to help them make the Kessel Run in enough time to bring the stolen unrefined coaxium to [[Savareen]] for refinement. Having learned that Calrissian was part of the operation, Weazel placed a tracking device on the ''Millennium Falcon'' so the Cloud-Riders could keep tabs on where Beckett and his team were ultimately headed.<ref name="Solo" />

The Cloud-Riders confronted Beckett's gang once they arrived on Savareen, and they engaged in a brief standoff. Nest ultimately explained the true motives of the Cloud-Riders, presenting Beckett's team with a choice about whether to hand the coaxium over to Crimson Dawn or allow the Cloud-Riders to take it and use the millions of [[Galactic Credit Standard|credits]] to attain their goals. As such, Solo and [[Qi'ra]] ended up killing [[Dryden Vos]] and a traitorous Beckett. Due to the actions and help of Han Solo, the Cloud-Riders acquired the coaxium. Weazel secured it in their transports as Nest told Solo what they wanted it for: to fuel a rebellion.<ref name="Solo" />

==Personality and traits==
[[File:Weazel_SWCT.png|thumb|right|200px|Weazel wearing his Cloud-Rider armor]]
Weazel was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] with [[Color|brown]] [[hair]], blue [[eye]]s, and light skin. Weazel, who stood shorter than most humans,<ref name="Solo" /> was once a common criminal for one of the five major crime syndicates but ultimately turned against them and believed in bringing justice to those throughout the [[galaxy]] who had been hurt by the syndicates and the Empire. As part of his operations, he carried a [[K21c portable ordnance launcher]] from [[Merr-Sonn Munitions, Inc.|Merr-Sonn Munitions]] and wore a [[Kalevalan tracker helmet]] that was equipped with a [[rangefinder]]<ref name="Solo Official Guide" /> and a device that enabled him to communicate with Nest.<ref name="Stickers">''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story Ultimate Sticker Collection]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|When we saw him in ''The Phantom Menace'' I think he was going off the rails a little but he was gambling and getting in the wrong crowd. I like to think that he maybe perhaps started to think 'well I need to do something good with my life.' and then started flying with a cause and that's when he joined Enfys Nest and got involved in that group. There's a bit in the middle there I haven't figured out yet, there's definitely a transition took place, but what the catalyst was for that I don't know.|Warwick Davis on Weazel's story after Episode I|<ref name="Weazel's Backstory">{{WebCite|url=https://www.cinemablend.com/news/2457866/what-happened-to-weazel-between-the-phantom-menace-and-solo-according-to-warwick-davis|text=What Happened To Weazel Between The Phantom Menace And Solo, According To Warwick Davis|date=2018-09-20|work=[[Wikipedia:Cinemablend|Cinemablend]]|archivedate=20200418211754}}</ref>}}
[[File:WeazelHS-TPM.png|thumb|left|200px|Weazel first appeared in ''The Phantom Menace''.]]
Weazel was first played by ''[[Star Wars]]'' veteran [[Warwick Davis]] in the [[1999]] film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], the first installment of the ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[prequel trilogy]].<ref name="Episode I" /> Davis reprised the role of Weazel for the [[2018]] [[Star Wars Anthology Series|''Star Wars'' Anthology]] ''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story]]''.<ref name="Solo" />

Davis was initially hired to only play the masked character of [[Wald]] in ''The Phantom Menace'', but director [[George Lucas]] decided during filming that he wanted Davis to appear onscreen unmasked. He accordingly placed Davis inside Watto's viewing box during the Podrace scene, and after [[Wikipedia:Artificial hair integrations|hair extensions]] were glued onto Davis's head.<ref name="SWArchive-starwars.com at Celebration III - Your Host: Warwick Davis">{{SWArchive|url=community/event/celebration/f20050419/indexp30.html|text=starwars.com at Celebration III - Your Host: Warwick Davis}} {{C|Additional [https://web.archive.org/web/20060104005003/http://www.starwars.com/community/event/celebration/f20050419/indexp30.html backup link]}}</ref> The scene was filmed over one day at [[Leavesden Studios]] in [[Wikipedia:England|England]], where, in Davis' own words, he was "basically sitting in bleachers and moving my head left to right."<ref name="When Artoo met Wicket">{{InsiderCite|39|When Artoo Met Wicket}}</ref>

''Solo'' co-screenwriter [[Jon Kasdan]] convinced his fellow screenwriter and father [[Lawrence Kasdan]] to bring Davis back as Weazel in ''Solo'', wishing to specifically include him as part of Enfys Nest's Cloud-Riders gang in order to meet Davis, given his love for Davis' role as [[W:c:willowufgood:Willow_Ufgood|Willow Ufgood]] in [[Lucasfilm]]'s classic [[1988]] film ''[[Willow (film)|Willow]]''. The elder Kasdan had no knowledge of Weazel due to not seeing the prequel films, but the younger Kasdan assured his father to trust him and let him write Weazel into the Anthology film.<ref>{{Lucasfilm|url=news/jon-kasdan-willow-interview|text=Jon Kasdan's ''Willow'' Adventure|date=2022-11-30|archivedate=20221204144116}}</ref> Weazel's costume in ''Solo'' was inspired by the signature [[Wikipedia:Imperial and Royal Hussars#Royal Hungarian Hussars|Hungarian Hussars]]' cavalry jacket worn by the English singer and musician [[Wikipedia:Adam Ant|Adam Ant]] in the early 1980s.<ref name="Art of Solo">''[[The Art of Solo: A Star Wars Story]]''</ref> Additionally, Davis revealed on his [[Wikipedia:Twitter|Twitter]] account that Weazel's costume included a piece of [[Ewok]] fur on his left shoulder, jokingly adding that the fur wasn't from [[Wicket Wystri Warrick|Wicket]], a character he portrayed in the [[1983]] film [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']].<ref name="Warwick Davis">{{Twitter|WarwickADavis|status/1018549388573016065|[[Warwick Davis]]|quote=Just discovered this cool image of #Weazel in #Solo. You've got the admire the skills of make-up and hair, costume design and prop making that come together to complete the intricate look. Note the Ewok fur on my left shoulder... #NotWicket|archivefile=File:Warwick Davis Ewok fur.png}}</ref>

Though Weazel's story between ''The Phantom Menace'' and ''Solo'' has yet to be revealed, Davis speculated on why Weazel left his life in the criminal underworld to join the Cloud-Riders: in his mind, Weazel realized that he was gambling and getting in the wrong crowd, leading him to think he needed to do something good with his life, though he doesn't know what caused Weazel's transition from criminal to freedom fighter.<ref name="Weazel's Backstory" />
